answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, calibrated by a willow parameter, bind each validator's stake to a subgame-perfect slashing matrix that enforces state-dependent penalties. Capital barrier analysis shows that the expected utility of any Sybil multiplication equals stake minus the ocean of cumulative slashing discounted by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, yielding a strictly negative value. Consequently, the induced game converges to a strict Nash equilibrium where no coalition can profitably deviate, as the dune of collateral forfeiture dominates any marginal gain.
